Fix: Entities and brackets stay on top inside a question
What was wrong: Both renderers already put brackets and entities above every other category — except inside a question, where a name that was ALSO a Theme or a Claim rotated through two colours. The same name rendered solid cyan four lines down the same page.
What it means for you: Your rule now holds everywhere: an entity or a bracket is on top of whatever category it sits on.

Fix: 44 addresses Q typed with a space are links again
What was wrong: 44 drops write "https:// wikileaks.org/…". Where the host began with "www." the address was still live; where it did not, 23 addresses were plain grey text. Worse, #866 rendered a link over "https:// wikileaks.org/" pointing at the SITE ROOT — a link that looks like it worked and goes to the wrong page.
What it means for you: Every one of those addresses is a single working link now. The text still shows Q's space; only the href drops it.

Fix: 238 comms strings are visible as unsettled
What was wrong: They were plain text in the drop and absent from every section.
What it means for you: They are in the Resolution Center, where the archive says what it has NOT settled. Nothing about them is asserted.

Fix: Entities and brackets render SOLID over another colour
What was wrong: The ordinary fills are translucent. Over another category the colour underneath tinted them, so a name inside a Claim came out neither cyan nor amber but a muddy third thing and you could not tell which layer was in front. 11,254 spans are in that position.
What it means for you: An Entity or a Bracket on top of anything is now opaque. Alone, it keeps the softer fill.

Fix: Every entity has a hover, and they all read the same way
What was wrong: The hovers were authored one at a time, so there were three sentence shapes — and 358 entities had no hover at all.
What it means for you: One pattern for all 1,532, built from the certified record. Expansions like "POTUS — President of the United States" are carried across verbatim, never invented. The per-post layer that says how ONE drop uses the label is untouched.

Fix: Q is Alice, except the sign-off
What was wrong: #74 and #78 write "Q = Alice" in Q's own words. The renderer paints a certified term wherever it appears, so the closing "Q" was being painted too — the one occurrence your ruling excludes.
What it means for you: 93 occurrences across 75 drops resolve to Alice; the sign-off is left alone; 65 homographs held.
